verses.1: Eliphaz the Temanite responded and said:
verses.2: Is your mind so full of words that none can silence you? Must you be so full of talk?
verses.3: Indeed, you have often corrected many, and your strong hands have supported the weak.
verses.4: You have raised the one who stumbled with a word, and you have strengthened the feeble with your knees.
verses.5: But now the calamity you sought has come upon you, and you are shaken.
verses.6: Is it not your fear that deceives you, your hope and the lawlessness of your ways?
verses.7: Recall now: who was pure and perished? Where were the upright ever destroyed?
verses.8: As I have seen those who plow iniquity, and those who sow trouble reap it.
verses.9: They are swept away by the command of God and consumed by the wind of His anger.
verses.10: The roar of the lion, the voice of the leopard, and the teeth of the lion are broken.
verses.11: The lion perishes for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lion are scattered.
verses.12: A word came to me in secret, and my ear received it by a whisper.
verses.13: It came to me in visions of the night, in dreams that fell upon men in sleep.
verses.14: Fear gripped me and trembling, and my bones were shaken.
verses.15: A wind came upon my face; my skin bristled and my flesh stood on end.
verses.16: It stood but I could not recognize it. Its form was before my eyes, yet I saw no face. I heard a voice.
verses.17: Is man just before God? Is a man pure in the Maker of him?
verses.18: Behold, even in His servants He does not trust, and His angels He charges with error.
verses.19: How much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before the moth!
verses.20: From morning to evening they are broken; without wisdom, they perish.
verses.21: Are they not brought forth only to die, lacking understanding?

notes:
Notes
- v. 16: The Hebrew is ambiguous whether the voice is divine or a vision; I have rendered it as a generic voice to avoid assuming the identity.
- v. 18: “charge with error” reflects the metaphor of God placing a stumbling block in the path of His angels, suggesting their fallibility. This is a metaphorical rendering.
- v. 19: “crushed before the moth” follows the Hebrew but may be a metaphor for fragility and insignificance.
